entries.title: France records 2,025 excess deaths at peak of heatwave as Europe braces for more extreme weather
entries.snippet: Forecasters are warning of further extreme temperatures on the continent in the next few days.

entries.title: On the Strait of Hormuz, BBC finds seized ships and shark fishermen as uneasy calm returns

entries.title: Venezuela quake survivor pulled out alive after eight days

entries.title: Nasa launches mission to save falling space telescope

entries.title: Iran begins public mourning for Ayatollah killed in February

entries.title: Instagram running ads promoting child sexual abuse material in India, BBC finds
entries.snippet: The ads use terms including “rape” and “child video” and link to content on the messaging app Telegram.

entries.title: A mayor in Japan announced her maternity leave - and got the whole country talking
entries.snippet: In the face of criticism, Shoko Kawata, 35, says she loves her job and is proud to be taking time off to have a baby.

entries.title: At least 32 dead after overcrowded bus plunges into ravine in Pakistan
entries.snippet: The bus was travelling from Quetta to Peshawar, when it crashed in the Dana Sar mountain range.

entries.title: 'Most massive' Russian attack on Kyiv kills at least 30
entries.snippet: The latest barrage deployed the largest number of weapons on the capital and hit locations over a wide area.

entries.title: Bomb blast at Damascus cafe kills nine, Syrian state media say
entries.snippet: There was no immediate claim for the bombing at a cafe close to the Palace of Justice, a major government building.

entries.title: Ebola treatments trial begins in DR Congo
entries.snippet: According to WHO data, there have been 1,406 confirmed cases of the disease in DRC, with 301 suspected cases and 438 deaths.

entries.title: Killers of British couple in South Africa sentenced to life
entries.snippet: The pair had been collecting rare plants and seeds before their bodies were found days later in a river.

entries.title: Canadian boy, 11, dies of rabies after waking to bat on his face
entries.snippet: Rabies infections are rare in Canada. There have been 28 human deaths due to rabies in the country since 1924.

entries.title: People smuggler convicted in France found by BBC living in UK and seeking asylum
entries.snippet: Once described as "the godfather" of French migrant camps, he has been working in a Leicestershire village.

entries.title: China says pilot crashed small plane into skyscraper for 'personal reasons'
entries.snippet: The 66-year-old, who died in the crash, had anxiety and referenced "ending his life" in his diary.

entries.title: Former Olympian indicted for allegedly vandalising Washington Reflecting Pool
entries.snippet: US authorities charged him with property destruction after renovations championed by President Donald Trump appeared to go awry.

entries.title: Nine Thai monks killed after 11-year-old driver collides with procession
entries.snippet: The group of 35 monks and five lay followers were walking by the roadside when the truck ploughed into them.

entries.title: South Africa and Ghana in diplomatic row over alleged killing of migrant
entries.snippet: South Africa denies claims that a Ghanaian citizen was killed in anti-migrant protests in Cape Town.

entries.title: Alleged Scattered Spider hacker arrested in Finland

entries.title: July 4th events threatened by heat wave. And, Russia strikes on Ukraine's capital
entries.snippet: July 4th events for America's milestone birthday are being threatened by a brutal heat wave. And, Russia has struck Ukraine's capital, killing several people in what it calls retaliatory attacks.

entries.title: Just gave birth or are about to? Share your story and questions about costs
entries.snippet: The costs of having a baby in the U.S. can be hard to predict and budget for. We want to hear your stories and questions about how to navigate the system.

entries.title: Former USAID head grieves its closure while hoping for its future
entries.snippet: Former USAID administrator reflects on a year since USAID's shutdown and the new direction of US foreign aid.

entries.title: But first, coffee: The drink that energized the American Revolution
entries.snippet: Colonial Americans were drinking coffee long before they dumped tea into Boston Harbor or fought a war for independence. The establishments that served it were already brewing revolutionary ideas.

entries.title: How a fertilizer shortage caused by the Iran war could affect U.S. food prices
entries.snippet: The closure of the Strait of Hormuz disrupted shipments of fertilizer and natural gas, a key component in fertilizer manufacturing. It's unlikely to cause major price hikes for U.S. grocery shoppers.

entries.title: How young people feel about American identity, on the nation's 250th birthday
entries.snippet: Listen to the best student podcasts about what "life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness" means for young people today.

entries.title: Oregon ER doctors win a 'David and Goliath' battle against a national company
entries.snippet: In a test of a new state law, doctors in Eugene went up against a national physician staffing firm seeking to replace them. Their success is getting attention across the U.S. as other states consider similar laws.

entries.title: A hot summer trend in the sharing economy? Rental swimming pools
entries.snippet: The Airbnb-style company Swimply said there have been about 275,000 private pool reservations so far this year.

entries.title: Morning news brief

entries.title: Heavy Russian strikes kill at least 21 in Kyiv after Ukrainian strikes disrupt Moscow's oil sector
entries.snippet: Russia hammered Kyiv in an 11-hour drone and missile attack overnight into Thursday morning, killing at least 21 civilians in the city and injuring scores more in what Moscow said was retaliation for Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil facilities.

entries.title: Grand jury indicts Louisiana's attorney general in fight over changes to local courts
entries.snippet: Louisiana's Republican attorney general was indicted Thursday on criminal charges by a grand jury in New Orleans, accused of trying to intimidate local officials who fought a law enacted by GOP legislators to overhaul the local courts.

entries.title: Russia pounds Kyiv with missiles and drones after Ukraine's strikes on oil infrastructure

entries.title: In Venezuela, a 'completely ineffective' government worsens earthquake disaster, experts say
entries.snippet: Hospitals lacking medicines and equipment. Daily power outages. At least 8 million people in need of humanitarian support. These were the realities in Venezuela before it was hit by back-to-back earthquakes on June 24.

entries.title: Europe's leaders close ranks as they face barbs and pressure from Trump
entries.snippet: After Trump questioned Italy's reliability as a wartime ally and claimed Giorgia Meloni had groveled for his attention, European leaders rallied to Meloni's side. It is the latest example of how the often divisive American president is helping to draw Europe closer together.

entries.title: Iran warns oil tankers to use approved routes in Strait of Hormuz or face a 'forceful response'
entries.snippet: Iran's joint military command warned Thursday that all oil tankers moving through the Strait of Hormuz must use its approved routes or face a "forceful response," ratcheting up tensions again over a waterway crucial for international energy supplies.

entries.title: WATCH: U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro announces felony charge related to Reflecting Pool
entries.snippet: A former Olympian was indicted Thursday on a felony charge in what President Donald Trump has called vandalism of the Reflecting Pool.

entries.title: Venezuelan medics fear earthquake aftermath will trigger widening medical crisis
entries.snippet: The emergency has laid bare Venezuela's chronic shortage of doctors, the result of years of economic crisis, underfunding and emigration.

entries.title: Gaza's future remains uncertain as Palestinians and Israelis mark 1,000 days of war
entries.snippet: It's the 1,000th day since a Hamas-led attack on Israel sparked the war in Gaza. Other conflicts have emerged in the region, and fragile ceasefires show scars of persistent attacks. Both Israelis and Palestinians are weary of the strain.

entries.title: The Onion's new parody of Alex Jones' Infowars starts with $100,000 to Sandy Hook families
entries.snippet: The families have still received no money from Jones since courts ordered him to pay more than $1 billion for falsely calling the 2012 shooting a hoax.

entries.snippet: The real estate mogul has become the billion-dollar crypto man.

entries.title: Some ransom notes sent in Nancy Guthrie case still being investigated as legitimate, FBI says
entries.snippet: The FBI did not specify how many ransom notes have been received, other than saying "several."

entries.title: Vatican excommunicates schismatic bishops and priests, and warns their followers
entries.snippet: The Vatican responded aggressively Thursday to a traditionalist group that consecrated bishops without the pope's consent, declaring the Society of St. Pius X had formally broken with the Catholic Church.

entries.title: An audacious climb turned into a marriage proposal. The couple was soon arrested
entries.snippet: Dressed in black and wearing masks but not tethers, the two balanced on a narrow ledge and appeared to kiss atop the New York skyscraper's antenna.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Germany: Voters are skeptical of reform proposals
entries.snippet: The German government is aiming to get the country back on track with a wide range of reforms. However, the latest Deutschlandtrend survey shows that the public remains unconvinced.

entries.title: Monaco IDs suspect in bomb attack on Ukrainian oligarch
entries.snippet: Authorities have issued an Interpol Red Notice and arrest warrant against a woman from Ukraine identified as suspect in a bombing that injured a Ukrainian-born businessman sanctioned by Kyiv and two other people.

entries.title: Moldova: Prime Minister Munteanu resigns
entries.snippet: Alexandru Munteanu announced his surprise resignation after just eight months as head of the government. President Maia Sandu said a successor would be appointed "quickly" in order to continue Moldova's pro-EU course.

entries.title: Iran: Dignitaries arrive for Ayatollah Khamenei's funeral
entries.snippet: Officials from China, Russia, India and other countries are in Tehran as Iran prepares to mourn the Supreme Leader, who was killed in an airstrike at the start of the US-Israeli campaign against Iran.

entries.title: Julian Nagelsmann out as Germany coach: The downfall
entries.snippet: The German Football Association (DFB) and national team coach Nagelsmann have parted ways after Germany's poor display at the 2026 World Cup.

entries.title: Germany news: Workers protest Mercedes-Benz cost-cutting
entries.snippet: Thousands of Mercedes-Benz workers across Germany are protesting the carmaker's cost-cutting drive. Meanwhile, firefighters rescued two window cleaners from a faulty platform high above Frankfurt. DW has more.

entries.title: India news: Indian delegation leaves for Khamenei's funeral
entries.snippet: A team of Indian delegates has left for Iran to attend the state funeral of Iran's former supreme leader Ayatollah Ali ​Khamenei. Follow DW for more.

entries.title: Pakistan: Bus crashes into ravine, killing at least 40
entries.snippet: Authorities say the overcrowded bus was likely speeding when it veered off a mountain road in Balochistan.

entries.title: Ukraine: Russia strikes kill 4 as Kyiv holds day of mourning
entries.snippet: The overnight strikes by Russia came a day after massive missile and drone attacks on Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, where a day of mourning is being observed.

entries.title: Man dies after setting himself on fire outside UN headquarters in New York
entries.snippet: A man has died after setting himself alight outside the UN headquarters in New York. Activists identified him as a Tibetan activist, though authorities have not confirmed his identity or motive.

entries.title: As heat waves loom, scientists wonder how humans will adapt
entries.snippet: Temperatures are set to soar in the US around the July 4 holiday, a week after Europe struck new records. With experts predicting more intense and more frequent heat waves in the future, can our bodies adapt?

entries.title: Taylor Swift, Travis Kelce set for star-studded New York wedding
entries.snippet: City permits point to a major star-studded celebration at Madison Square Garden over the Fourth of July weekend, although the celebrity couple has not confirmed the event.

entries.title: AI drones made in Germany see duty on Ukraine's front line
entries.snippet: The German defense company Helsing is supplying combat drones to Ukraine and will soon provide them to the German army. How effective are they on the front line? DW joined a Ukrainian combat mission to find out.

entries.title: Venezuela leader rejects criticism for earthquake response
entries.snippet: Acting President Delcy Rodríguez has slammed critics for saying her government was slow to respond to the disaster. She said the criticism was "manufactured in propaganda laboratories."

entries.title: South Africa, Ghana clash over migrant's death
entries.snippet: The two countries are embroiled in a diplomatic dispute following the death of a Ghanaian national in South Africa this week. It comes amid rising tensions in South Africa over undocumented migration.

entries.title: Russia launches attacks on Kyiv, killing at least 27 and injuring scores
entries.snippet: Ballistic and cruise missiles and drones were used in what Kyiv's mayor, Vitali Klitschko, said was the largest attack on the city since the war began.

entries.title: After heat wave: Wildfires ravage southern France
entries.snippet: Firefighters battle several wildfires in southern France that were fueled by strong winds. Nearly 3,000 tourists and locals were evacuated.

entries.title: Venezuelan man rescued alive 8 days after powerful quakes
entries.snippet: Rescuers worked around the clock for three days to free security guard Hernan Gil from the rubble of the building where he worked.

entries.title: Albanian police fire tear gas at 'Flamingo Revolution' rally
entries.snippet: Albanians have continued to protest against a planned luxury resort backed by Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner. They say the resort threatens the coast's fragile ecosystems, including a flamingo habitat.
